grounding.claim: I8 'Project source' is an interface the product exchanges data through with Git
grounding.note: Line 50 is the single `subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(repo), ...])` helper every git read goes through, and its callers ask git for the MAPPED project's content: `blob_lines` runs `git show <sha>:<path>` (impact_git.py:122) and `changes_between` runs `git diff` (impact_git.py:166). What comes back is the user's own source and history, which the product never wrote, so this is data crossing in from outside the product, not its own output read back.

grounding.claim: I9 'Code editor' is an interface the product exchanges data through with Code editor
grounding.note: `doOpenSource` calls `editorUri(n.file, n.line)` and, at line 14925, `fireUri(uri)` — which creates an anchor and clicks it, navigating the browser to a scheme URI. `editorUri` (14868-14881) fills a template with `{abspath}` = the reader's local source root + the mapped path, plus line and column, and only allows a scheme in ALLOWED_OPEN_SCHEMES. So a file path and a line leave the product for a separate desktop application; the editor is the far side, not a pipe.

grounding.claim: I10 'Code host' is an interface the product exchanges data through with GitHub
grounding.note: Line 14928 is `window.open(gh, '_blank', 'noopener')` on the URL built by `ghUrl` (14897-14904): the saved/build-time repo URL plus `/blob/<commit>/<path>#L<line>`, with `ghRef()` (14891) reducing the map's commit field to a real sha. The page fetched at that URL is served by the code host, not by this product, so the far side is GitHub itself.

grounding.claim: I11 'Coding agent chat logs' is an interface the product exchanges data through with Coding agent chat logs
grounding.note: Line 130 globs `CLAUDE_PROJECTS` — `Path.home() / '.claude' / 'projects'` (line 40) — for `<session-id>.jsonl` transcript files, and the module then reads their contents (`_cwd_of_transcript` opens the jsonl at line 141; `_WRITE_TOOLS` at 138 scans the recorded tool calls). Those files are written by the coding agent's own harness, never by this product, so this is data crossing in from a store the product does not own.

grounding.claim: I1 'Command line': R1 'Map owner' is on its far side
grounding.note: cli.py:166-168 dispatches the typed word `serve` to `serve.main(rest)`; the file is the argv-driven entry point installed as the `coyomap` console script (pyproject.toml:36-37). A person typing `coyomap serve` or `make install` (Makefile:70) is the one on the far side, and that person is the map's Map owner — the human who wants a map of their own project.

grounding.claim: I2 'Method quality command line': R3 'Method author' is on its far side
grounding.note: cli.py:73-75 dispatches the typed word `run` to `run.run_cli(rest)`, and `coyomap-eval` is a console script (pyproject.toml:37 `coyomap-eval = "coyomap_eval.cli:main"`), so a human types it. run.py's own header (lines 2-5) says the run scores a built map against the blessed baseline — the question the Method author has, and the Makefile calls the eval skill a developer surface "not meant for a user of coyomap" (Makefile:104).

grounding.claim: I3 'Map viewer': R1 'Map owner' is on its far side
grounding.note: The claim carries no anchor, so I read the server's routing. serve.py:639-642 serves INDEX_HTML at `/` and routes `/api` to `_root_api` — the landing page, described at line 910 as "add a project by browsing to its folder, or to open / remove a recent one". grounding.claim: I3 'Map viewer': R2 'Map reader' is on its far side

The page it serves is the browser viewer (viewer.js) whose whole job is showing a map's tabs, cards and code links to someone reading it. So the reader is on the far side of this interface; I moved the line, not the verdict.

grounding.claim: I4 'Build skill': R1 'Map owner' is on its far side

Makefile:70-76 copies this exact file into each agent's skills home with the clone path substituted, so it becomes the `/coyomap` command a person invokes. grounding.claim: I5 'Developer skills': R1 'Map owner' is on its far side

Makefile:102-108 says the eval and retro skills are opt-in, and verbatim: "neither is meant for a user of coyomap" and "installing the developer surface should never be a side effect of setting up the tool" — which is why `install-dev` (Makefile:107) is separate from `install` (Makefile:70). The Map owner is the map's USER actor; the README never mentions install-dev or coyomap-eval at all. The far side of the developer skills is the Method author (eval/SKILL.md:28, EP2), and the map's own I5 record is facing "operator". The join looks to have carried UC1's single actor onto steps that belong to the method author.

grounding.note: Line 28 tells the agent to read `__COYOMAP_HOME__/eval/method.md` and follow it end to end; Makefile:82-88 installs this file as the `coyomap-eval` skill, and Makefile:102-104 states the eval answers "did my change make the maps worse?" and is a developer, not user, surface.
